title: Cartesian scheme-test line families and their morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A test is a scheme $W$ over $S$ with a map $h_W\to X$. A line family assigns an ordinary invertible module $P_W$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and an isomorphism $j^*P_V\simeq P_W$ to every test map $j:W\to V$, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Coherence means the identity and composition equations using the canonical pullback comparisons [def-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-iso]. An etale line presentation also specifies a line module $L$ on the small etale site of $X$ and additive equivalences $\Gamma(W,P_W)\simeq L(W)$ for all small etale tests, linear over regular functions and natural for etale restrictions. Test-family morphisms are families $e_W:P_W\to Q_W$ commuting with all the pullback comparisons. A morphism induces $f:L\to M$ when its action on the global sections of every small-etale test, under the specified equivalences, is the component of $f$. Test-family isomorphisms and their compatibility are defined by the same equations. Identities and compositions act componentwise.
